updates.statement: Accuracy noise sets the usable margin, and decisions near the gate select for luck. Revised noise model: the 3-seed scored mean has a run sd of ~0.2 pp (E101: identical code gave 0.7561 vs 0.7516), and per-seed sd is 0.22-0.38 pp. Rerunning the same seed in a new process moves accuracy about as much as a cross-seed draw does (E028; cuDNN-pick divergence), so pairing by seed barely reduces variance. The SE of a one-process 22-seed off-seed difference is ~0.10-0.11 pp, not the 0.05 claimed in E098. Every off-seed delta since E096 is therefore <1.2 SE: E100 +0.09, E102 0.00, E103 +0.02, E104 +0.12, E105 +0.09. Rules: bit-identical reruns count once. A keep or a close needs >=3 fresh processes per arm on seeds 3-26, or >=2 distinct scored samples plus multi-process off-seed. Support and refutation use the same threshold. The loop broke these rules with E090, E096 and E100, each kept on a favorable first draw. Current tip E100: distinct scored 0.7561/0.7516 (mean 0.7538, n=2), so the local gate is met in ~60% of reruns, partly by luck. No config is robustly feasible yet. E095's support is one off-seed process plus a scored pool that mixes different code. The official 40-seed bar (0.75) is probably cleared by the whole lineage (~0.751-0.753).
updates.reason: Review: same-seed cross-process divergence breaks the pairing, so the claimed SE was wrong, and E101 shows run sd ~0.2 pp. Restated around the E100 tip and noted that E096/E100 repeated the luck-selection pattern.

updates.statement: Run-to-run noise (~0.2 pp sd on a 3-seed mean; ~0.1 pp per off-seed process), not cross-seed std, is the decision-relevant noise floor. Picking whichever near-threshold variant first clears 0.753 selects for luck. This happened with E026, E046, E068, E090 (distinct mean ~0.7515-0.7524), E096 (bit-identical second scoring; off-seed +0.17 in one process and -0.11 in another, E098) and E100 (0.7561, then 0.7516). Every comparison must pool distinct samples across >=3 processes per arm.
updates.reason: Adds E096 and E100 as further cases and corrects the noise magnitudes (E098, E101).

updates.statement: Extended off-seed instrument and tip decision. Run the unchanged E090 config and the E095 config on seeds 3-26. Prediction: E090's mean is <=0.7530 and E095's is >=0.7540. Outcome: E098 confirmed E090 at 0.7525, but it ran E096 instead of E095, in one process per arm. The claim that E095 is the robust fallback has never been measured. Superseded by N4.tip (>=3 processes per arm).
updates.reason: The E090 half held. The E095 half was never run, and one process per arm cannot resolve 0.1 pp. The 'refutes' verdict came from the scored row, not from the stated prediction.

E094: sd of the 8-seed mean across distinct processes is ~0.09 pp, inside the predicted 0.07-0.15. E098 (0.25 pp gap for the same code on seeds 3-10) confirms that past single-process off-seed deltas are <1.5 SE.

updates.statement: Provenance check, untimed and free. Still to do: (1) git-diff E077-E084 against their stated base; (2) resolve E092/E093 (idea names E086, outcome says E090); (3) resolve the newer mismatches: E103 was specified on E090 but ran on E100; E105's idea says E090 code but its outcome says E100, so it is unclear whether 0.28 was applied globally on top of the 32 px x1.25 (an effective 0.35 at 32 px) or replaced it. Recompute the affected off-seed deltas against the correct baselines. Any mismatch removes the run from its A/B.
updates.reason: New base ambiguities in E103/E105 matter for interpreting H10.2 and H7.1.3.

updates.statement: Part of the run-to-run variance might be a per-process offset shared by all trials, from the cuDNN pick set. Current evidence does not require it. E098's 0.25 pp gap on the same 8 seeds and E101's 0.45 pp scored gap are consistent with iid per-seed divergence (~0.17 pp sd expected for an 8-seed rerun difference). Kernel-name logs were requested in E081/E094/E098/E099 but never analyzed. Analyze the existing logs (no runs). If pick sets do not cluster with run means, retire this and treat all run noise as iid within-seed divergence, which only more processes reduce.
updates.reason: Review: the per-process offset is not required by the data, and the decisive logs are already available.

updates.statement: Per-epoch GPU work drives the score. Tip: E100 (2@16 + 1.25@24 at bs 1536, then 1.25@28 + 2.75@32 at bs 1024, Fable tail with the final window pinned to 8 steps, 32 px Muon lr x1.25, pinned staging) at ~4.46 s. Distinct scored samples are 0.7561 and 0.7516 (mean 0.7538), so it is likely feasible partly by luck (H4). Every measured accuracy/time trade runs at ~0.04-0.065 pp per 1%: the 32 px trim (E089), the 28 px substitution (E090), bs 1024 at 32 px (E084/E095) and bs 1024 everywhere (E104). With ~0-0.05 pp of real margin, schedule and batch reshuffles have converged. The possible exception is the 24 px bridge, which may trade at ~0.13 pp per 1% (H8). Closed time levers: CUDA graphs/launch (E052), Inductor tuning (E066), cuDNN determinism (E036), cudnn.benchmark_limit (E099), prepare (E060, E086), group-2 width cuts (E080), whitening-bias freeze (E093), 32 px trims and the 28 px substitution. Remaining FLOP levers, all to be profiled untimed first: depth cuts (H2.18) and a tile-aligned group-3 width (N2.19). Cost structure: the 32 px phase is ~71% of time and energy-bound; 16 px is low-occupancy.
updates.reason: Restated around the E100 tip. Added the E099 closure and the E104 exchange rate, and added the new tile-alignment lever from search.

updates.statement: Compile, graph and transfer configuration was a FLOP-neutral time lever, and it is now exhausted. Banked: static per-resolution graphs (-2.0%, E053), max(dim).values instead of AdaptiveMaxPool2d (-2.9%, E056; amax gives NaNs under torch 2.4 Inductor, E055), and a pinned staging buffer (-0.5%, E086/E087). Closed: cudnn.benchmark_limit=0 (E099, +0.2%; the default 10-algorithm search already finds the best kernels), Inductor pointwise tuning (E066) and the build dress-rehearsal (E076).
updates.reason: E099 closed the last untested candidate.
E099: time +0.2% (4.477 s vs ~4.46 s), build 270 s; below the pre-registered 0.3% closure bar. Math-neutral, so the time verdict does not depend on accuracy noise.

updates.statement: Per-phase batch size. Large early batches hurt (E043: bs 2048 at 16/24 px, -0.49 pp, warmup-confounded). Smaller batches in the 32 px phase help: bs 1024 there gave +0.12-0.18 pp scored and +0.10-0.11 pp off-seed (E084/E085/E095, each one off-seed process) at +2.5% time. E095 pinned the EMA window and kept the gain, so the effect is update count, not window length. bs 1024 everywhere (E104, one process) bought a similar amount per added step, so the rate is ~0.04-0.065 pp per 1% wherever the steps go. That only matches what trims cost and cannot fund a net cut. Porting the window pin to E090 (E096) gave +0.17 off-seed in one process and -0.11 in another (E098), so it is unresolved.
updates.reason: Adds E104's rate and the conflicting E096/E098 evidence.

updates.statement: Ablation of E084's confound: pin the final-EMA window and lookahead stop to the last 8 steps under bs 1024 at 32 px. E095 (on E070 + pinned staging): off-seed 0.75405, equal to E084's 0.7541, which supports update count over window length. The port to the E090 tip (E096) is unresolved: scored 0.7539 twice (bit-identical, so one sample), off-seed +0.17 in I102's process and -0.11 against E090 in E098's process. The window pin carried into E100 therefore has no net multi-process support.
updates.reason: Review: E096 was kept on one effective sample and later contradicted; the E095 part still stands on one process.

updates.statement: Extend the bs-1024 tail to bs 768 in the 28/32 px phases (E100 base; samples-indexed; SGD by the kilostep rule; Muon unchanged; window pinned to 8 steps; static shapes warmed in build). Pre-registered time: +3-4.5%. Prediction: off-seed gain >= +0.25 pp over >=3 processes per arm, i.e. above 0.065 pp per 1%. A gain <= +0.12 pp closes the per-phase batch line. Low prior: E104 shows added steps buy ~0.04 pp per 1% anywhere. bs 768 at 32 px also gives M = 6912 = 54 tiles of 128, i.e. 2.5 waves on 108 SMs (search: NVIDIA wave quantization), so per-step efficiency drops.
updates.reason: E104's rate lowers the prior, and the search's wave-quantization analysis adds a time penalty.

updates.statement: Depth cuts as a time lever. Width cuts failed because of tile quantization (E080). Removing a conv removes whole cuDNN kernels and ~23 elementwise kernels, so the saving should be close to proportional. In airbench96 each group is conv1 -> pool -> BN -> GELU, followed by a residual branch conv2 -> BN -> GELU -> conv3 -> BN added to the post-pool x0 (search: airbench96.py). So a depth cut must be defined as a 1-conv residual branch or as dropping the branch. Approximate conv MACs per image at 32 px: g1 conv1 27M, conv2/3 33M each; g2 conv1 100M, conv2/3 65M each; g3 conv1 98M, conv2/3 27M each. Group 2's conv3 is the largest single cut (~14%); g1 conv3 (~7%) touches the largest activation traffic (31x31x128), and g3 conv3 (~6%). External prior is weak: airbench95 (2 convs, no residual) does about half the per-epoch FLOPs, but no isolated ablation exists. Capacity is valuable on CIFAR-100 (E017, E050).
updates.reason: Search corrects the depth-cut design (residual structure, group-2 target).

updates.statement: Untimed first. On the E100 net, profile per-step time and NVML energy at 32 px and 28 px (bs 1024) and at 24 px (bs 1536) for three variants, each reducing one group's residual branch to a single conv plus the skip: (a) group 2 (~14% of conv MACs), (b) group 1 (largest elementwise traffic), (c) group 3. Prediction: at least one variant cuts projected total run time by >=6% over the E100 schedule. Score only that variant, with the 32 px phase lengthened to spend half the saving (net ~-3%). Decide on >=3 off-seed processes per arm, within 0.05 pp of E100. If no variant saves >=6%, close depth cuts without a scored run.
updates.reason: Search showed group 2's conv3 is the largest target and that 'remove conv3' was ambiguous under the residual structure.

updates.statement: Optimizer quality per update was the binding constraint on CIFAR-100 at ~7-8 epochs, and Muon was the lever: +1.14 pp at equal epochs (E019), a flatter epoch slope (E020), large-batch tolerance (E022, E038). Head on Muon and head lr 0.5x are each worth ~+0.1-0.2 pp on weak evidence. Closed: momentum (flat 0.5-0.6; external work finds momentum schedules cost -1.7 pp on CIFAR-100, search 2603.28921), NS count, cheaper orthogonalizers (MUD/NorMuon are weaker per step and untested on CNNs), head lr/wd. Muon lr on the mixed-batch tip is untested: 32 px x1.25 (E100) and peak 0.28 (E105, base ambiguous) each gave +0.09 pp off-seed in a single process, inside the ~0.1 pp SE. Schedule shape (WSD/cosine vs linear) has never been tested under Muon (N7.4).
updates.reason: Folds in E100/E105 as inconclusive under the corrected SE, plus the external momentum and orthogonalizer evidence.

updates.statement: Muon momentum and lr sit at a flat local optimum. Momentum is flat in 0.5-0.6 and steep above (E027, E030). LR was flat in 0.20-0.24 on the bs-1024 E026 base (E034). On the mixed-batch tip, a higher lr (E100 32 px x1.25, E105 0.28) moved off-seed by +0.09 pp in one process each, which is noise-level. No lr change is established in either direction.
updates.reason: Records the E100/E105 transfer tests as noise-level.

updates.statement: Raise the conv-filter Muon peak lr from 0.24 to 0.28 in every phase. Prediction: off-seed >= +0.1 pp. Outcome E105: +0.09 off-seed (one process, SE ~0.1), scored 0.7525. The base is ambiguous: the idea names E090 and the outcome says E100, so 0.28 may sit on top of the 32 px x1.25. Neither supported nor refuted. Retest only together with H10.2.1, on a clean base with >=3 processes per arm.
updates.reason: Review: E105's +0.09 was called noise while E100's identical +0.09 was called support. Under one consistent threshold both are inconclusive.

updates.statement: On the Muon tip, at fixed epochs and resolution split, adding optimizer updates raises accuracy at ~0.04-0.065 pp per 1% of time, apparently regardless of placement. Evidence: bs 1024 at 32 px (E084/E085/E095: +0.1-0.18 pp for +2.5%) and bs 1024 in all phases (E104: +0.12 off-seed for +2.8%, one process, with a scored 0.7525 that disagrees in sign). Removing steps costs accuracy (E038, E022). The rate equals what time cuts cost, so update count is not a net lever at the current margin. Open: whether the 32 px gain is Muon path length or update count (H10.2; E100/E105 inconclusive).
updates.reason: E104 leans toward placement-independence but is single-process; the path-length test is inconclusive.
E104's off-seed gain sits inside H10.1.1's predicted band but comes from one process, and the scored row disagrees. Leaning supported, not established.

updates.statement: On the E100/E090 config, run 16/24 px at bs 1024 too (+~53 low-res steps). Prediction (placement-independent): off-seed gain +0.05 to +0.15 pp. Outcome E104: +0.12 off-seed (one process, SE ~0.1), scored 0.7525 (-0.13 pp vs the tip's scored pool), time +2.8%. The result is inside the predicted band, so it leans toward support. With a single process and a scored row of the opposite sign, it is not decisive.
updates.reason: Review: the token was inverted. The result fell inside the predicted band, so it is E104~ (leaning supports), not E104-.
Its only test (E100) is inconclusive under the corrected SE, and the matched global-lr arm (E105) gave the same +0.09, so phase-local vs global cannot be told apart.

updates.statement: Raise the conv-filter Muon lr by x1.25 in the 32 px phase only (run on the E090 base, a deviation from the E086 spec). Prediction: off-seed >= +0.08 pp at equal time. Outcome E100/E101: off-seed +0.09 paired vs the E096 baseline (one process; corrected SE ~0.1), scored 0.7561 and 0.7516 (distinct mean 0.7538). E105 (global 0.28, base ambiguous) gave the same +0.09. Not established. Re-decide in N4.tip with >=3 processes per arm, and add a matched global-lr arm on E090 to separate phase-local path length from 'just a higher lr'.
updates.reason: Review: a +0.09 inside a ~0.1 SE is not support. E100 was kept on a favorable first draw.

updates.statement: Accuracy at the tip is bounded by late training at test resolution (32 px samples x updates in the final phase), not by total steps or epochs. The evidence is weak. The 32 px trim (E088/E089 pool 0.7522) and the equal-step 28 px substitution (E090, ~0.7515-0.7524) are equal within ~0.01 pp, which cannot separate 'exposure binds' from 'total updates matter'. E104 leans toward placement-independence. E102 (stem bias trained into the 32 px phase) was null. The direct discriminating test against the rival view, that the 24 px bridge is worth more per second (H8), is N8.2.1.
updates.reason: Review: the core evidence is a null difference inside noise, E104 points the other way, and E102 was null.

Only the 70% arm was run (E102: 0.00 off-seed, +1.2% time). The never-freeze arm would also pay the stem dgrad and its expected value is low. E093's large loss is better explained by early-phase fragility (H8) than by switch adaptation. Retired on expected value; the mechanism was not cleanly refuted.

updates.statement: Move the whitening-bias freeze from ~41% to ~70% of samples, with never-freeze as a second arm. Prediction: the best arm gains >= +0.1 pp off-seed. Outcome E102 (70% arm only): off-seed 0.00 vs tip (one process), scored 0.7521, time +1.2%. The never-freeze arm was skipped, so the pre-registered closure condition (both arms within ±0.05) was not met.
updates.reason: Only one of two arms was run, in a single process, so the outcome is closer to a refutation than an inconclusive result in direction but does not meet the closure rule.
E104 (one process) leans against the claim that low-res steps buy nothing.

updates.statement: Same run as H10.1.1, opposite prediction: an off-seed gain <= +0.03 pp from ~53 added low-res steps; a gain >= +0.08 refutes it. Outcome E104: +0.12 off-seed (one process, SE ~0.1), scored -0.13 pp vs the tip pool. Leans toward refutation, but this needs a multi-process replicate.
updates.reason: Review: it had no token even though E104 tested it. E104~ leans toward refutation.

Scalar knobs and end-of-run averaging are exhausted. H6.5.4 is inconclusive (E103: +0.00 vs E090, +0.02 vs tip, inside its pre-registered dead zone, and run on E100 rather than E090). Retired on expected value, not because the BN-mismatch mechanism was refuted. Structural data-side accuracy levers move to the new Lvl1 NA.
The tail stays in the code (E068/E069, E079 ablation). Longer windows did not help with copied buffers (E081, E083) or with averaged buffers (E103). Retired on expected value.

updates.statement: Use a 20-step final EMA with BN running stats lerped alongside the weights instead of copied from the net. Prediction: >= +0.05 pp vs E090 off-seed; <= -0.05 would close end-of-run averaging. Outcome E103 (run on E100, not E090): off-seed +0.00 vs E090 and +0.02 vs tip (one process), scored 0.7535. The result is in the dead zone. Compared with E081's -0.09 with copied buffers, buffer averaging moved the 20-step window by ~+0.1 pp, weakly toward explanation (b), BN mismatch. Not worth further runs.
updates.reason: Review: the pre-registered refutation needed <= -0.05; the result was 0.00/+0.02, and it ran on a different base.

updates.statement: Asymmetric early-training sensitivity. Removing early-phase quality is very costly: no 24 px bridge -0.68 pp (E032), bs 2048 early -0.49 (E043, warmup-confounded), whitening bias frozen at ~3% -0.44 off-seed and -0.5 scored (E093), and the 24 px bridge trim cost ~0.14 pp per 1% (E070, against a lucky pool). Adding early steps returns only about linearly (E104: +0.12 off-seed for +2.8%, one process). Implications: the 24 px bridge is the highest-value phase per unit time, no further 16/24 px cut should be tried, and time moved from the 32 px phase into the bridge may add accuracy (N8.2).
updates.reason: Review: the three largest clean negative effects since Muon are all early-phase interventions, which is the strongest structural signal in the tree. Reinstated in a reformulated, asymmetric form.

new.statement: Re-decide the tip lineage with the corrected instrument. Free step first: compute the within-seed cross-process sd from the existing E028/E094/E098 per-seed logs and checksums. Then, untimed through the benchmark's trial code, run E090, E096 (window pin), E100 (window pin + 32 px Muon lr x1.25) and E095 (bs 1024 at 32 px on the 4@32 schedule) on seeds 3-26, in >=3 fresh processes each. Predictions: (1) within-seed cross-process sd >=0.2 pp, so seed pairing reduces variance by <30%; (2) pooled E100 - E090 < +0.1 pp, i.e. the +0.09 single-process estimates were noise; (3) pooled E095 - E090 >= +0.08 pp, i.e. the bs-1024 32 px gain is the one replicated lever. If E100 - E090 >= +0.1 pp with SE <=0.06, E100 is banked and H10.2 gains support. If E095 is not >= +0.08, no config is robustly feasible and accuracy must be found before any further cut.

The 24 px bridge buys accuracy at about twice the rate of the 32 px phase. E064/E065 vs E062/E063: +0.12 pp for +0.9% time (~0.13 pp per 1%). E070's trim: -0.25 pp for -1.8% (~0.14 pp per 1%, against a lucky pool). The 32 px trim (E088/E089) cost ~0.065 pp per 1%. If this holds, moving time from the 32 px phase into the bridge at equal total time adds accuracy. H11 (late full-res binds) predicts the opposite, so this is the direct discriminating test.

On E100 code, run 2@16 + 1.75@24 (bs 1536) + 1.25@28 + 2.5@32 (bs 1024): +0.5 epoch at 24 px funded by -0.25 epoch at 32 px. Switches, LR, floor-hold and tail are indexed by samples; the window stays pinned to the last 8 steps; all shapes are already warmed in build. Pre-registered time: within ±1% of E100 (0.5 x ~0.52 s vs 0.25 x ~0.9 s plus step-count change). Prediction (H8): pooled off-seed gain on seeds 3-26 >= +0.1 pp over >=3 processes per arm, and two distinct scored samples not below E100's distinct mean. If the gain is <= -0.05 pp, H11's late-full-res claim beats the bridge-value claim and N8.2 is refuted.

Under Muon, per-batch data composition and augmentation, not scalar optimizer knobs, are the remaining zero-time accuracy sources. Every augmentation test (E008 brightness/contrast, E016 crop vs resize) ran under SGD, and the loss and regularization tests were scalar. Muon fits ~1.1 pp better and the tail adds averaging, so the balance between regularization and gradient variance has moved. Fort et al. 2021 (search) report that augmentation variance, not just the augmentation, harms generalization on CIFAR-100. To fund another ~5% cut, a lever must show >= +0.15 pp pooled over >=3 off-seed processes at unchanged time.

Multi-sample augmentation at equal compute. Drawing 2+ augmented copies of the same image within a minibatch, with batch size and step count fixed, lowers test error, and on CIFAR-100 the benefit saturates near 4 copies. The optimal LR is unchanged at large batch. Risk at ~7 epochs: unique-image coverage in the affected phase is halved.

On E100, in the 32 px phase only (bs 1024), build each batch from 512 unique images x 2 independent augmentation draws. Translate offsets are drawn independently per copy; the alternating-flip copy keeps its scheme and the second copy gets the opposite flip. Samples per step, step count and shapes are unchanged, so time stays within ±0.5%. The 32 px phase then covers ~1.4 unique epochs instead of 2.75. Prediction: pooled off-seed gain on seeds 3-26 >= +0.1 pp over >=3 processes per arm. If it is <= -0.15 pp, data coverage dominates at this budget and the line closes.

Class-balanced minibatches. With ~10-15 images per class per batch over 100 classes, a uniform permutation leaves per-class counts per batch highly variable. Stratified batches reduce gradient variance from class imbalance at zero compute, which may matter in a ~280-step run.

On E100, replace each epoch's uniform permutation with a stratified one: every batch holds floor or ceil of bs/100 images per class in random order, generated on the GPU from the trial seed inside train, so no data touches import or build. Samples, steps and shapes are unchanged; time within ±0.3%. Prediction: pooled off-seed gain on seeds 3-26 >= +0.1 pp over >=3 processes per arm. A result within ±0.05 pp closes it.

Augmentation strength under Muon. Translate magnitude was never tuned, and late-phase regularization was never tested under Muon. Muon's faster fitting may now leave room for stronger geometric augmentation in the final full-resolution phase, even though under SGD more augmentation did not help (E008).

On E100, raise translate from 2 to 4 px (reflect padding, same fused GPU op) in the 28/32 px phases only, leaving the low-res phases unchanged. Time within ±0.5%. Prediction: pooled off-seed gain >= +0.1 pp over >=3 processes per arm. If it is <= -0.1 pp, the short budget is under-fitting under Muon too, and augmentation strength is closed.

Group-3 width set by tile alignment. Convs run as implicit GEMMs. Group 3's 576 channels = 4.5 x 128, so with 128-wide N tiles every group-3 GEMM (fwd N=K, dgrad N=C, wgrad M=C*9) already pays for 640. Widening to 640 would then add capacity at near-zero conv time (only ~11% more group-3 elementwise work at small 7x7/3x3 maps), while 512 could save more than its FLOP share. This is consistent with E080 (352/320 recovered only 33-60%).

Free first: read the logged cuDNN/cutlass kernel names for the group-3 convs at 28/32 px (E094/E099 logs). If they use 64-wide N tiles, close without runs (576 = 9x64 wastes nothing).
